subject: Exploring annual prepay for BrightGrid - staggered commit & indexation
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@brightgrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightGrid Procurement <procurement@brightgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring annual prepay for BrightGrid

Hi Hannah,

Hope you’re well. We’re evaluating moving BrightGrid from monthly billing to an annual prepay for 2027+. Our procurement team asked me to reach out to understand what Redwood supports for multi-year commitments and what concessions you can offer for an upfront payment. A few specific asks from our side: 

- Can you do a staggered upfront schedule (50% upfront / 50% later) instead of a single lump-sum?
- Do you offer multi-year discounts (we’re considering 2–3 year terms) and are discounts step-down or flat?
- Is Redwood open to indexation (CPI or similar) in later years, or do you prefer fixed pricing?
- We need ramp protection: if we don’t hit committed usage early, what credits/true-ups exist?
- Legal is going to ask about early-termination exposure — we need guardrails.

We are targeting a decision by mid-November. Can we set up a quick call this week to go over options? I’ve attached our expected run-rate and current monthly spend for reference.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | BrightGrid Inc.

Attachment: brightgrid-runrate-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@brightgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring annual prepay for BrightGrid

Julia — thanks for the context and the forecast. Happy to run through options. Quick answers up front: we can support staggered upfront schedules, multi-year term discounts, and a couple of different models for ramp credits/true-ups. Indexation is possible but typically applied from year 2 onward rather than the first year.

Suggested next steps:
- 30-minute call to confirm target committed volumes and preferred invoice cadence (single invoice vs split).
- I’ll follow with a draft commercial proposal that captures a few variants (12-mo fixed, 18-mo staggered prepay, 24-mo with modest CPI indexation).

I’ve attached an initial CTA-level proposal to frame the pricing conversation. Can you do Friday 11/30 at 9am PT? If not, suggest two windows.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: initial-cta-proposal.pdf (proposal stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@brightgrid.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Draft commercial structures for BrightGrid — pricing matrix attached

Julia / Hannah — following our call last week I built three concrete options in the attached spreadsheet (BG-pricing-matrix.xlsx). High level: 

Option A — 12-mo fixed (no indexation)
- 12-month term, single upfront invoice
- 10% discount to list based on 12-mo commit
- No indexation
- True-up at year-end; customer pays/receives adjustment

Option B — 18-mo staggered prepay (recommended for ramping customers)
- 18-month term, staggered payments: 60% up front, 40% at month 10
- 12% effective discount in year 1 (front-loaded benefit)
- Indexation applies from month 13 tied to US CPI (month-over-month) with floor 0% and cap +4% annually
- Ramp protection: if usage in first two quarters is <60% of committed, we issue service credits equal to 10% of shortfall (applied to invoice or as future credit), subject to a true-up cap of $75,000 across the term
- Early-termination for convenience: liquidated-damages equal to remaining committed value less prepayments received; we can discuss a carve-out for force majeure

Option C — 24-mo committed (best unit economics)
- 24-month term, 50% upfront / 25% @ month 9 / 25% @ month 15
- 15% average discount across term
- Year-on-year CPI indexation with a +/-1% collar from projected CPI baseline (more complex to operationalize)

A few notes on indexation and early termination: indexation helps us maintain economics over multi-year deals for pricing-sensitive models; if procurement requires fixed pricing, we can keep year 1 flat and only apply an agreed formula in subsequent years. Regarding termination, we typically limit damages to a cap (we proposed $75k above) but can tighten.

Attached: BG-pricing-matrix.xlsx (pricing matrix)

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet with procurement/legal and adjust wording for the term sheet.

—Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@brightgrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft commercial structures for BrightGrid — pricing matrix attached

Team — thanks for sending. Procurement and finance reviewed the matrix. A few counterpoints from BrightGrid: 

1) Indexation: we are not comfortable with an open CPI tie without a tighter band. For budgeting purposes we need predictability. Proposal: fixed price for first 12 months; indexation only in year 2, capped at +2% and floored at 0%.

2) True-up cap: $75k is high relative to our expected run-rate (we forecast ~$600k ARR on Redwood at steady state). Can you bring the cap down to $40k or add a tiering model (lower cap for year 1)?

3) Invoice cadence: we prefer quarterly invoices (we cannot approve a full single upfront payment through our ERP without extra approvals). If Redwood needs cashflow protection, we can do 50% upfront + quarterly invoicing for the remainder.

4) Early termination: we need a commercial cap (max 3 months of committed spend) rather than open-ended liquidated damages.

5) SOC2 & evidence: procurement requires SOC2 Type II and a summary of retention/audit logs. Please attach.

If you can get these changes into a term sheet we’ll fast-track legal review.

Marcus
Marcus Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager | BrightGrid Inc.
procurement@brightgrid.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@brightgrid.com>, Julia Park <julia.park@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft commercial structures for BrightGrid — pricing matrix attached

Marcus / Julia — thanks for the clear feedback. We talked with finance and legal and propose the following compromise to address your constraints while preserving fair economics for Redwood: 

Commercial compromise (term-sheet highlights):
- Term: 18 months
- Payment schedule: 50% upfront, 30% at month 7, 20% at month 13 (this supports your ERP needs while giving Redwood earlier cashflow)
- Year 1: fixed pricing (no indexation)
- Year 2 (months 13–18): indexation tied to US CPI with a cap of +3% and floor 0% (we can tighten further to +2% if required but +3% gives us a bit of runway)
- True-up / ramp credits: if usage in first two quarters is <65% of committed, Redwood will issue credits equal to 12% of the shortfall amount for Q1–Q2 only. Credits are applied to outstanding invoices or as an account credit. Total true-up credit cap = $50,000 for the 18-month term.
- Early termination for convenience: capped to 3 months of committed spend (after accounting for prepayments received).

Attachments included: term-sheet-v3.pdf (reflects the language above) and SOC2-summary.pdf. We can publish a redline in DocuSign for a one-click acceptance flow: https://docusign.example/sgn/abcd1234

If this is acceptable we’ll get a formal DocuSign ready and queue up finance for the invoice schedule. Laura will own invoicing and will send the requested invoice cadence options.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0133

Attachments: term-sheet-v3.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

From: Julia Park <julia.park@brightgrid.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft commercial structures for BrightGrid — pricing matrix attached

Laura / team — this language looks good and addresses the procurement concerns. One small redline request: please ensure the CPI indexation only applies starting month 13 (i.e., no retroactive adjustments) — I believe that’s already how it’s written, but legal asked for explicit confirmation.

If you can publish the DocuSign with that explicit clause we’ll run a quick legal sweep and sign. Happy to finalize today. Thanks for working through the compromises.

Julia
Julia Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | BrightGrid Inc.
